<p class="eyebrow">Get started / Installation</p>

# Install Flux. {#install-flux}

::: {.doc-lead}
One command puts the workspace on your machine. A short setup window takes care of the extras you need.
:::

::: {.availability-note role="note"}
**The first desktop release is being prepared.** Flux v0.2.0 is currently a draft. The command below is ready for the public release, but **cannot install Flux until that release is published**. Follow [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/releases) for availability. Developers can [run Flux from source](#from-source) today.
:::

## One line to install {#install-command}

Open **Terminal** on macOS, or your terminal on Linux, and paste:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fluxsci.github.io/install.sh | bash
```

<div class="platform-line"><span>macOS · Apple Silicon &amp; Intel</span><span>Debian / Ubuntu · x86-64</span></div>

The installer downloads the latest public release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, installs Flux, and opens it. On macOS, it uses `/Applications` or your user Applications folder. On Linux, it installs a `.deb` through `apt`, which may ask for your password. It adds one marked line to your shell profile so new terminals can find the `flux` command.

[Read the installer](/install.sh){.text-link} · [View its source on GitHub](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/install.sh){.text-link}

Windows and other Linux distributions do not yet have a supported installer.

## Set up what you need {#setup}

The first launch opens **Set up Flux**. You can return to it through **Settings → General → Setup**, or search **Set up Flux…** in the command palette.

| What you want to do | What to set up |
|:---|:---|
| Compose figures, present slides, read PDFs, or export a PDF from Flux | Ready in the app. |
| Export a Word document or use `flux compile` | Install **Quarto** from the setup window. |
| Build a PDF through Quarto or `flux compile --to pdf` | Add **TinyTeX** from the setup window. |
| Make semantic plots in Python | Add **fluxplot** to your analysis environment. |
| Work with Claude Code or Codex | Install and sign in to your agent, then connect it through the **AI agents** row. |

Quarto and TinyTeX are optional. Flux's own PDF export works without either. The setup window installs companions in your user folders and checks for tools you already have.

### Add fluxplot to an analysis environment

In an existing [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) project:

```bash
uv add fluxplot
```

For 3D mesh exports:

```bash
uv add "fluxplot[mesh]"
```

Using another Python environment? Run `pip install fluxplot` there. For a new uv project, run `uv init` first. Fluxplot belongs beside your analysis code; each plot's recipe records how to regenerate it.

### Connect your AI collaborator

Open **AI** in the Flux titlebar, choose **Connect** for your agent, review any proposed replacements, then restart open agent sessions. The connection panel provides the command to start working with a particular project. [Read the agent connection guide](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/docs/agents/connect.qmd).

## Check the installation {#verify}

Open a **new terminal** after installing:

```bash
flux version
```

This prints the installed build. If you connected an agent, check its setup with:

```bash
flux connect doctor
```

To check fluxplot from your analysis project:

```bash
uv run python -c "import fluxplot; print('fluxplot is ready')"
```

## Keep Flux up to date {#updates}

Run the installation command again to update to the latest public release. Flux can also check for updates once a day; turn that check on or off in Settings.

On macOS, **Update now** waits for Flux to close, replaces the app, and reopens it. On Linux, Flux offers the update command to copy, because `apt` may need your password.

To choose a specific **published** release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fluxsci.github.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.2.0
```

The v0.2.0 example becomes usable once that release is public.

## If something needs attention {#troubleshooting}

<details class="doc-details"><summary>The command cannot find a public release</summary>

The first release is still in draft. The installer cannot download draft assets anonymously. Check [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/releases) and try again when a release appears there.

</details>

<details class="doc-details"><summary>My terminal says “flux: command not found”</summary>

Open a new terminal so the installer’s PATH change takes effect. If the command is still unavailable, open **Set up Flux → flux in the terminal** to install the launcher.

</details>

<details class="doc-details"><summary>Word export or a Quarto PDF will not build</summary>

For Word, install Quarto in the setup window. For `flux compile --to pdf`, add TinyTeX too. Journal PDF styles may also need TeX packages or an SVG converter; the [companion-tool reference](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/docs/installation.qmd#extras-for-journal-styled-pdf) lists those requirements. Flux’s own PDF export remains available without this setup.

</details>

<details class="doc-details"><summary>The installer reports a checksum mismatch</summary>

No app was installed. Run the command again to download a fresh copy. If it persists, check the release’s published checksums and report the problem in [Flux issues](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/issues).

</details>

<details class="doc-details"><summary>I want to uninstall Flux</summary>

On macOS, delete Flux from the Applications folder where it was installed. On Linux, run `sudo apt remove flux`. Your projects and `~/FluxConfig` remain in place. Keep that folder if you want to retain your library, context, and reusable plots.

</details>

## Run from source {#from-source}

Contributors and early testers can run the current source checkout with **Node.js 22.15 or newer**:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fluxsci/flux
cd flux
npm ci
node node_modules/electron/install.js
npm run electron:dev
```

The Electron download is a separate step. A source checkout is also needed for the separate [Lighttable companion](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/docs/lighttable.qmd).
